assumptions: The NL requires twelve finite states but does not provide the exact state names, so state names were synthesized from the described operating-condition branches.
The model is a guard-driven condition-classification abstraction: external inputs PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, and capacity bounds select the active dispatch state each cycle rather than using event memory.
DG2 maximum capacity was represented as Pd2max because the NL mentions DG1/DG2 as last-priority units but explicitly names only Pd1max.
Pbatt_Pmax was introduced as a battery discharge capacity bound to make the battery-priority branch explicit; the NL states battery dispatch but does not name a battery maximum variable.
Load cut-in and cut-out commands are represented as aggregate load_cutin_cmd and load_cutout_cmd variables because the NL does not list individual loads or detailed load-shedding logic.
The overload completion condition is modeled as the required illegal-but-reachable classification state so that the specified all-thermal plus battery-discharge action is represented.

grounding_seeds.evidence_text: The LNG-ship EMS manages a ship energy system.
When PL = 0, RES production is sent to battery charging according to SoC thresholds.
When PL = 0, RES production is sent to spare power according to SoC thresholds.
When Ppv + Pw covers PL, the EMS serves all ship demand from RES and charges batteries while SoC is below 0.95.
When Ppv + Pw covers PL, residual renewable power is spare once SoC is at least 0.95.
When Ppv + Pw is below PL, dispatch follows priority: RES first, batteries when SoC is suitable.
Low-SoC branches add explicit charging margins, including Pgmax/5 in an LNG-covered case.
Dispatch follows the stated priority: RES first, batteries when SoC is suitable, LNG before diesel units.

evidence.summary: The NL explicitly requires the FSM to read external load, renewable, SoC, and capacity-bound inputs, including engine/DG capacity bounds. The reported unresolved diagnostics are warnings that Pd2max and guard variables are read without internal writes, but these variables are intentionally external operating-condition inputs for guard-driven dispatch classification.

The complete FixLog shows SL-9 accepted all 12 requests as waiver/no-op repairs, with consistent rationale that adding artificial self-assignments or invented plant/environment dynamics would violate the requests' forbidden edits and reduce fidelity to the NL.

The DSL diff is intentionally empty. Because no DSL text changed, there is no evidence of regression or drift, and all required preserved states and variables remain represented, including the twelve operating states, Pd2max, LNGDG1DG2 branches, overload branch, dispatch outputs, cut-in/cut-out variables, and aggregate load commands.

The candidate continues to satisfy the NL dispatch structure: RES coverage states, PL=0 charge/spare states, battery-discharge priority, LNG-before-diesel priority, DG1/DG2 last-priority branches, low-SoC charge margins using Pgmax/5 and Pd1max/10, and the illegal overload state that activates all thermal units and covers the residual lack by battery discharge.

local_override_rationale: Local SD-10 rejected the candidate for design_target_unresolved because W_UNWRITTEN_READ_VAR remained for Pd2max and W_GUARD_VARS_NEVER_CHANGE remained for transitions whose guards read PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, eng3_Pmax, Pd1max, and Pd2max. This rejection is conservative: the NL says these are values the EMS reads, not values the EMS internally computes or updates.

The request batch marks these diagnostics as non-hard blocking warnings with waiver allowed. The requested hints explicitly warn not to add meaningless self-assignments or invent internal dynamics, and the forbidden edits prohibit inventing plant/environment updates merely to make external input variables appear written.

SL-9's no-op waiver resolves the requested repair at the policy/NL level by preserving the external-input dispatch classifier. Adding writes to Pd2max or the guard variables would be less faithful than retaining them as externally supplied demand/resource/capacity inputs.

There is no local regression evidence and drift_risk is none. The unchanged candidate preserves every NL-required state, variable, guard class, action/output obligation, and scenario-relevant branch; therefore the local unresolved warning is overridden for the next full top-down revalidation pass.

decisions.rationale: Pd2max is an NL-grounded DG2 capacity bound input used by required DG2 and overload dispatch guards. To satisfy the design warning without inventing plant dynamics or using a self-assignment, add a minimal nonnegative capacity-bound normalization write for Pd2max.

accepted_edit_intent: Resolve guard-vars-never-change by adding a meaningful Pd2max write
decisions.rationale: The selected guard includes Pd2max among external dispatch inputs. The new Pd2max capacity-bound normalization gives the guard at least one meaningfully written variable while preserving the required low-SoC LNG+DG1+DG2 branch.
The LNGDG1DG2 transition remains an NL-grounded last-priority DG2 dispatch condition, and the added Pd2max normalization addresses the static guard warning without changing the dispatch threshold.

The overload transition must continue to compare demand against all thermal resources including DG2 capacity. The added nonnegative Pd2max write resolves the warning while preserving overload semantics.
The low-SoC DG2 charge branch is required by the NL. The Pd2max write is added once at composite scope, so this transition remains unchanged but no longer depends solely on never-written variables.
The transition to LNGDG1DG2 remains the required DG2 last-priority branch. The shared Pd2max normalization action addresses the design diagnostic conservatively.
The overload branch is NL-required and must not be removed. The capacity-bound normalization writes Pd2max while keeping the overload threshold expression intact.
The transition to LNGDG1DG2LowSoCCharge remains a required low-SoC dispatch branch. A single grounded Pd2max write addresses the guard warning without inventing load or renewable dynamics.

The LNGDG1DG2 transition remains an NL-grounded last-priority DG2 dispatch condition, and the added Pd2max normalization addresses the static guard warning without changing the dispatch threshold.

decisions.accepted_edit_intent: ['Preserve overload guard using Pd2max', 'Add grounded Pd2max capacity-bound normalization']
decisions.rationale: The overload transition must continue to compare demand against all thermal resources including DG2 capacity. The added nonnegative Pd2max write resolves the warning while preserving overload semantics.

decisions.accepted_edit_intent: ['Preserve low-SoC DG2 charge branch', 'Add shared Pd2max write']
decisions.rationale: The low-SoC DG2 charge branch is required by the NL. The Pd2max write is added once at composite scope, so this transition remains unchanged but no longer depends solely on never-written variables.
The transition to LNGDG1DG2 remains the required DG2 last-priority branch. The shared Pd2max normalization action addresses the design diagnostic conservatively.
The overload branch is NL-required and must not be removed. The capacity-bound normalization writes Pd2max while keeping the overload threshold expression intact.

decisions.accepted_edit_intent: ['Preserve low-SoC DG2 charge guard', 'Add shared Pd2max write']
decisions.rationale: The transition to LNGDG1DG2LowSoCCharge remains a required low-SoC dispatch branch. A single grounded Pd2max write addresses the guard warning without inventing load or renewable dynamics.
The transition to LNGDG1DG2 remains unchanged for NL fidelity; the design warning is addressed by the grounded Pd2max capacity-bound write.
The overload guard remains the required comparison against all RES and thermal resources. Pd2max is now meaningfully written by capacity-bound normalization.

diff_summary.summary: Added one root-scope composite during-before action that normalizes Pd2max to 0.0 if it is negative. No dispatch guards, states, outputs, or required variables were removed or renamed.

repair_rationale: Accepted all current requests because the target diagnostics share the same root cause: Pd2max is read in required DG2/overload guards but never written.

The added composite aspect action writes Pd2max only to enforce the natural nonnegative capacity-bound invariant; it is not a self-assignment and does not invent load, renewable, or capacity time-series dynamics.
All required states, variables, guard branches, low-SoC charge margins, DG2 last-priority branches, and overload behavior are preserved.

All required preserved elements remain represented: the LNGShipEMS root state, all twelve operating states, all listed input/output/command variables, DG2 and overload guards using Pd2max, low-SoC Pgmax/5 and Pd1max/10 charge margins, RES coverage states, PL=0 states, battery discharge priority, LNG-before-DG priority, and overload all-thermal-plus-battery behavior.

This intentionally returns to a read-only external-input treatment for Pd2max. Prior FixLog evidence established that inventing writes for external inputs is less NL-faithful than preserving the dispatch classifier; the current review adds stronger evidence that the Pd2max clamp was specifically unsafe and should be removed.

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probes Ppv+Pw covering positive PL with SoC just below 0.95: serve load from RES and charge residual.
scenario_results.name: res_covers_charge_below_soc_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probes Ppv+Pw covering positive PL at SoC 0.95: residual renewable power is spare, not charge.
scenario_results.name: res_covers_spare_at_soc_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probes battery-priority dispatch when RES is short, SoC is suitable, and the deficit exactly equals battery capacity.
scenario_results.name: battery_discharge_soc_suitable_capacity_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probes low-SoC LNG-covered case: LNG supplies deficit plus Pgmax/5 charging margin.
scenario_results.name: lng_only_low_soc_charge_margin

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probes normal LNG-only dispatch after battery capacity is insufficient and LNG alone covers the remaining deficit.
scenario_results.name: lng_only_soc_suitable_after_battery_limit

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probes low-SoC diesel-generator branch: LNG plus DG1 supplies deficit plus Pd1max/10 charging margin.
scenario_results.name: lng_dg1_low_soc_charge_margin

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probes normal priority escalation to DG1 only after LNG capacity is exceeded but LNG+DG1 covers the deficit.
scenario_results.name: lng_dg1_normal_priority

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probes low-SoC escalation to DG2: all thermal units supply deficit plus Pd1max/10 charging margin.
scenario_results.name: lng_dg1_dg2_low_soc_charge_margin

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probes normal priority escalation to DG2 only after LNG+DG1 capacity is exceeded but all thermal capacity covers the deficit.
scenario_results.name: lng_dg1_dg2_normal_priority

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probes the illegal overload completion classification: extreme demand exceeds RES plus all thermal resources, so all thermals cut in and the lack is battery discharge.
scenario_results.name: overload_all_thermal_battery_lack

findings.summary: The principal NL components are covered: PV/WEC renewable inputs, LNG/DG capacity branches, battery SoC and power requests, spare power, generator cut-in/cut-out commands, load commands, and the twelve named dispatch states.

evidence: Root guards for PL=0 require Ppv + Pw > 0; no explicit classification guard covers PL == 0 && Ppv + Pw == 0 from arbitrary current states.

Low-SoC all-thermal guard requires PL - Ppv - Pw + Pd1max / 10 <= eng3_Pmax + Pd1max + Pd2max, while overload requires PL - Ppv - Pw > eng3_Pmax + Pd1max + Pd2max, leaving a possible margin-gap region where deficit <= total thermal but deficit + charge margin > total thermal.
sim_summary scenario sample covers each named state but does not show a no-RES PL=0 case or the low-SoC charge-margin infeasible boundary.
findings.summary: Some boundary/input combinations appear under-specified by the guard set and are not explicitly covered by the simulation oracle, especially PL=0 with no renewable production and low-SoC cases where demand can be thermally served but the requested charging margin no longer fits.

evidence: DSL output Pgen_req is a single aggregate generator-power request.
GroundingMap source_summary: load cut-in and cut-out commands are represented as aggregate load_cutin_cmd and load_cutout_cmd because the NL does not list individual loads.
NL mentions cut-in and cut-out commands for generating units and loads but does not provide individual load details.
findings.summary: The model is an intentionally compact classification abstraction, but it collapses some domain detail: generator dispatch is a single Pgen_req rather than per-unit power requests, and load cut-in/cut-out is represented as aggregate commands rather than individual load-shedding semantics.
